title: The treatment-side credit-result record has no operation, no element names, no state values and no column rule in the S2 sources
source: Legacy RWB-E2-006 (04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epic 2 Story Files v5/RWB E2 006 Credit approval pack for NLEADS v1.md), sections 3, 4, 5, 7, 9, 11, 12, 13 and 14; FSD S2 TDR, settlement and deed in lieu v3 A1.2 (FEAT-TRT-01 to FEAT-TRT-18), A2.1 to A2.18 and the Screens table; TSD S2 TDR, settlement and deed in lieu v2 T1, T3.0, T3.1 (DF-TRT-011 and DF-TRT-023 to DF-TRT-026), T3.2, T5.1 and T-A.1 and T-A.2 (API-S2-001 to API-S2-004); Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-01, DP-03, DP-07, DP-11 and DP-15, R7.2
section: 1 Story; 3 Preconditions; 4 Flow; 5 Exception paths; 7 Acceptance criteria AC1 to AC9; 8 Business rules; 9 State transitions; 11 Data; 12.1; 12.2; 13 Solution plan; 14 Validation and messages; 15 Screens and states
description: One combined row for the story. (1) No S2 source carries the credit-result record itself: the FSD S2 decomposition A2.1 to A2.18 and the TSD S2 appendix T-A.1 (API-S2-001 to API-S2-004) hold the treatment resource, the draft-terms change, the submit and the offer, and no operation that records a NLEADS result, because the legacy story sat in the P2 Integration module. The result write therefore sits on the PATCH of the treatment resource, whose element set is the TreatmentUpdate of the draft-terms change and not a credit-result payload. (2) The element names of that credit-result variant are given by no source; only the legacy request members (nleadsRef, result, approvalLevel, resultDate, reason) and the length rules exist. (3) The treatment state values SUBMITTED, APPROVED and REFUSED are stated only in the legacy section 9 body text: TSD S2 T3.0 gives the standard state column with no list and TSD S2 T3.2 publishes LOV-TRT-OUTCOME (KEPT, BROKEN, COMPLETED, CANCELED, DECLINED) for the separate outcome column, so the state values and their check constraint are a working read. (4) The four credit columns are given in the legacy section 13 and in TSD S2 T3.1 as DF-TRT-023 to DF-TRT-026, but no source states their nullability at NLEADS time, the rule that a reason is present only when the result is REFUSED, the rule that credit_result_at is set only with credit_result, or the uniqueness of one result per treatment; the legacy story leaves all of them to a migration of the treatment owner. (5) The validation messages of the write are the legacy MSG-GEN-001 and MSG-GEN-002, while the state refusal of the treatment row has no message of its own: the legacy story uses MSG-P3-005 for the case route state, and this story reads the same text on the treatment state. (6) The reference and reason formats are given only as lengths and a Character set (1 to 30 letters, digits and dashes, assumed until SCB IT confirms under DL12) and no source publishes an NLEADS reference pattern.
evidence: TSD S2 v2 T3.0 (standard state column, no list), T3.1 (DF-TRT-011, DF-TRT-023 to DF-TRT-026), T3.2 (LOV-TRT-OUTCOME without SUBMITTED, APPROVED or REFUSED) and T-A.1 (API-S2-001 to API-S2-004 only); FSD S2 v3 A1.2 and A2.1 to A2.18 (no credit approval record) and Screens (SCR-14 lists no field); legacy RWB-E2-006 sections 9 (SUBMITTED to APPROVED or REFUSED), 11 (the four columns), 12 (CreditResult members and the If-Match header), 13 (the four new treatment columns, the reason check, no P2 table) and 14 (MSG-GEN-001, MSG-GEN-002, MSG-P3-005)
owner_role: Solution architect, S2, with the rwb-treatment tech lead and the rwb-integration owner
proposed: The treatment contract baselines of this service add the credit-result variant of the PATCH and its element names at the wave 2 contract freeze, with the If-Match header and the once-only rule; the standard state column gains a check constraint that carries SUBMITTED, APPROVED and REFUSED; the four credit columns are added on the service's own Flyway sequence with the reason rule, the result-date rule and the length checks; one result exists per treatment, enforced by the credit_result_at value and the version guard; and the state refusal of the treatment row is given its own message in the message register or MSG-P3-005 is confirmed for it.

title: The rwb-treatment share of the key is stated by no S2 source, and the caller contract, the level comparison, the case move and the record ownership are split across four stories
source: Legacy RWB-E2-006 sections 4, 7, 10, 12, 16 and 18; Template and Rules v1 R5.4, R5.5 and R5.7; _work/msr/context/S2.md (S2 ownership rows: four REST operations, one event EV-10, no jobs, one workflow TreatmentWorkflow); Recovery Workbench Service Story Files v1 RWB P2 E2006 APP (the integration side of the same legacy key, sections 1, 12.1 and 12.2); RWB-S2-E3001-CON and RWB-S2-E3002-CON (the treatment resource and its PATCH)
section: 1 Story; 3 Preconditions; 4 Flow; 8 Business rules; 10 Authority; 12.2; 12.3; 12.5; 12.6; 12.8; 13 Solution plan; 15 Screens and states; 16 Test cases; 18 Traceability; 19 Out of scope
description: One combined row for the split. (1) The split is the one RWB-P2-E2006-APP states in its own section 1 and section 12.2, where it names the treatment read and the treatment PATCH as the two calls it makes; no S2 source states which part of legacy RWB-E2-006 the treatment service keeps, so the boundary is read from the sibling story, the ownership rows and the two contract baselines of this service, and is recorded here. (2) The shapes, the fakes and the two integration-base operations belong to the P2 slice and are unpublished at the time of writing, so this story builds against a caller fake and no C row is claimed in the plan, although DP-07 adds RWB-P3-E1043-CON. (3) The level comparison with the delegation of authority of item 2.1.1 and its refusal MSG-P2-018 are answered by the caller and by rwb-access, so this story stores the level as given; the legacy values are also inconsistent (AC2 records L5 for a plan the Background sets at L6 or higher, AC7 refuses L6 for a plan that needs L5) and no source settles which of them is right. (4) The route state AWAITING_CREDIT_APPROVAL, its move by R-RES-11, R-RES-12 and R-RES-14, the case owner's queue and the case-side record are rwb-case's share and no S2 source states it. (5) The record is written locally once per service that changes its own state, so one NLEADS decision now produces a record at the caller and at this service, sealed in order by the P7 ledger; no source states how many records one decision produces or in which order they are sealed. (6) This service publishes no event type of its own for the key: EV-10 TreatmentApproved is the event of the treatment and offer stories and the ownership rows grant no second event, so only the library record publication is written. (7) SCR-14 now composes a case read, a pack and a treatment read; the field list, the route and the merge rule belong to the edge contract and no S2 source publishes them.
evidence: _work/msr/context/S2.md ownership rows (REST 4 provided, events 1 EV-10, jobs 0, workflow TreatmentWorkflow) and naming rules; RWB P2 E2006 APP section 1 (the pack, the submission and the two integration-base operations) and section 12.2 (GET /api/recovery/treatment/v1/treatments/{treatmentId} and PATCH /api/recovery/treatment/v1/treatments/{treatmentId}); RWB-S2-E3001-CON section 12.1 and RWB-S2-E3002-CON section 12.1 (the treatment resource, the PATCH and the TreatmentUpdate element); legacy RWB-E2-006 Background, AC2, AC7, sections 4, 9, 10 and 12 (DelegationQuery, CaseEvents.raise, DecisionLogWriter); TSD S2 v2 T4 (R-RES-11, R-RES-12, R-RES-14) and T6.1; Template and Rules v1 R5.4, R5.5 DP-03, DP-11 and DP-19, R5.7
owner_role: Solution architect with the rwb-integration, rwb-treatment, rwb-case and rwb-access tech leads and the gateway-bff owner
proposed: The split is confirmed as written in this story when the P2 and P3 slices publish their contracts; the two operations of the treatment resource and the credit-result element set are recorded in the Service Contract Catalog against rwb-treatment; the level comparison, its message and the delegation version are recorded against rwb-access and the caller; one ledger entry per record and its sealing order are recorded against rwb-decision; and the SCR-14 merge of the case read, the pack and the treatment read is recorded against the edge contract.
